title: SPML Infra Ltd - 500402 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: SPML Infra Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 20% YoY to INR238.7 crores, with H1 operating cash flow of INR82.4 crores versus a INR44.1 crore outflow.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue was INR238.7 crores (up 20% YoY), EBITDA INR26.3 crores (up 33%, margin 11% vs 10%) and PAT INR22.2 crores (up 46%, PAT margin 9.3%). H1 revenue was INR505 crores (up 45%), H1 EBITDA INR55 crores (up 33%) and H1 PAT INR45 crores (up 64%). Cash generation was the main highlight, with H1 operating cash flow of INR82.4 crores and cash and equivalents up 88% to INR119 crores. Order inflow commentary was softer: management said Q2 was affected by water tender slowness and monsoon months, and the order book stood at about INR5,056 crores as of 26 September 2026.

financial_highlights.change: vs outflow of INR44.1 crores in H1 FY26
up 88% from INR63 crores at March 2026
increased on profit accretion and warrant conversion of legacy obligation of about INR700 crores

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Water remains the largest segment, about 65-70% of the order book per management's split. Tendering was uneven in H1; large schemes such as PKC link, Ken-Betwa, Wainganga-Nalganga and NVDA projects are expected to tender by March 2027. Management said JJM dues are being cleared and JJM 2.0 orders are coming with fund clarity; SPML said it has no direct JJM exposure.

segments.name: Power T&D and substation
segments.commentary: Management said power (including the BESS NTPC order) is about 30-35% of the order book. Recent win: INR186 crores from Power Grid for Bhadla-III and Ramgarh substation extension, the company's entry into 765 kV EHV work. Management expects similar orders this fiscal year.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: NTPC Barauni BESS order of INR1,128 crores has design and drawing approvals; management expects about INR300 crores of revenue in FY27, starting H2. Pune plant is at Phase 1 with 2.5 GWh capacity, targeting 5 GWh by H1 FY28; a 600-container facility is also being built. Proprietary 104.4 kWh battery pack has international certification; OEM battery-pack business is being developed alongside EPC.

guidance_outlook: Revenue and PAT growth guidance of at least 25% for FY27 unchanged; management said FY27 will exceed guidance, with H2 revenue and profitability expected above H1.
FY27 order inflow guidance of about INR5,000 crores retained; management said securing this will not be a challenge.
Management expects new orders won in FY27 to generate revenue only from FY28, since design and drawing approvals take 6-9 months.
Growth of about 25% per year on top line and bottom line expected for the next few years, to be updated annually based on order book and pipeline.
Pune BESS capacity to reach 5 GWh by H1 FY28; longer-term expansion to 5-10 GWh possible, with Pune land (about 25 acres) sized for up to 10-20 GWh.
capex_capacity: BESS manufacturing at Pune: Phase 1 operational at 2.5 GWh; target 5 GWh by H1 FY28, per management's comments.
BESS container manufacturing facility (600 containers) started; expected completion in H1 FY28. NTPC order containers to be partly sourced from own plant; future BESS containers to be fully in-house.
Pune site has about 25 acres of land, which management said can be expanded to 10-15-20 GWh.
Order book about INR5,056 crores as of 26 Sep 2026; only about INR1,161 crores is legacy, and the rest is largely projects with expected operating margins of 10% or higher.
Management said the INR5,000 crore FY27 inflow target includes JV share.
demand_pricing: Management said it bids only on contracts with price variation clauses and avoids fixed-price tenders. Management said it does not bid below 10% expected margin, and that commodity and FX moves have not materially hit BESS margins.
BESS tenders are strong across PSUs and non-PSUs; management said over INR8,000 crores of tenders have been bid, with one more EPC conversion targeted in FY27 (order size INR500-1,000 crores).
Management said the government is reviewing the pricing mechanism for fixed-price BESS contracts, which have come under cost pressure across the industry.
Legacy orders are mostly subcontracted back-to-back, carrying lower margins and minimal working capital; management said there is no residual BG, LD or performance exposure.
O&M: management said EPC to O&M split is about 95:5 by value, and that O&M margins are higher than EPC margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why no new BESS orders since the NTPC order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is bidding actively on PSU and non-PSU tenders, expects one more EPC conversion in FY27, and is also pursuing OEM battery-pack orders with shorter turnaround.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise its 25% growth guidance after strong H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the at-least-25% guidance unchanged for now, citing H2 being stronger than H1 due to monsoon-constrained H1 activity, and said it expects to exceed guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is operating cash flow sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flow is healthy when projects are fully funded with design approvals in place, and expects positive operating cash flow to continue as the order book shifts to such projects.

qa_highlights.question: How are commodity price increases affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids projects without price variation clauses, so margins are protected; BESS contract has a price variation provision and the recent price moves were not material.

qa_highlights.question: What is the arbitration award position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR100 crores of awards across two matters are at a very advanced stage, with settlement expected soon; this would reduce debt. Management also cites total arbitration claims of about INR3,827 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 order inflow reach INR5,000 crores, and what is the water/power split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR5,000 crore target is on track, the order book is about 65-70% water and 30-35% power including the NTPC BESS order, and JV share is included.

risks_watch: Order inflow pace: Q2 inflow was soft, and water tendering has been uneven; FY27 target of INR5,000 crores depends on water schemes tendering by March 2027 and on BESS conversions.
Execution timing: NTPC BESS revenue of about INR300 crores in FY27 depends on the Pune plant and containers, which are still ramping, and new orders take 6-9 months to start revenue.
Government fund flow: management acknowledged possible near-term liquidity pressure on government schemes, including JJM underspend of about INR20,000 crores to date.
Legacy order book of INR1,161 crores is expected to complete in FY27-FY28, at lower margins, and management gave no quantified execution schedule.
Arbitration monetisation: about INR370 crores of legacy obligation is backed by an arbitration award of about INR655 crores with interest; settlement timing for the INR100 crore awards is not fixed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, cash flow and margin protection, but cautious on order inflow and timing. Management repeatedly gave no firm dates for tender conversion or arbitration settlement, and deflected on some questions (for example, C&I BESS participation and the water/power split was given only in approximate ranges).
key_quotes: Our guidance of at least 25% growth remain unchanged for now, and we will keep you updated in our quarterly calls.
We prioritized fully funded project in cash-rich states, and that is now showing up clearly in our cash flows.
We do not bid for projects without a price variation clause as we have strategically decided not to take risk on factors outside our control, such as commodity price and foreign exchange.

adds.what: Pune BESS manufacturing expansion from 2.5 GWh (Phase 1 operational) to 5 GWh

growth.why: FY27 revenue and PAT growth of at least 25% held (not raised), with management saying FY27 will exceed it and H2 above H1; backing is a ~INR5,056 crore order book and a Pune BESS expansion to 5 GWh (H1 FY28, about 2 quarters out for the 600-container facility), but new FY27 orders only contribute from FY28 and Q2 order inflow was soft, so backing is partial.

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR238.7 crores and H1 revenue rose 45% to INR505 crores, but the brief does not state whether growth was volume, price or mix, and it names no one-off gain, loss or low base in the year-ago quarter.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose to 11% from 10% and management won't bid below 10% expected margin on new projects, with H2 profitability guided above H1 and BESS margins not materially hit by commodity moves.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pune BESS Phase 1 is operational at 2.5 GWh with the 5 GWh target set for H1 FY28 and a 600-container facility under construction with completion in H1 FY28, both firmly committed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth of at least 25% held and management expects H2 above H1 (H1 revenue INR505 crores, up 45%), though Q2 order inflow was soft and new FY27 orders only contribute from FY28.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The Pune site has about 25 acres that can be expanded to 10-20 GWh, and management spoke of a 5-10 GWh longer-term expansion, but no new capex amount or date has been announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management kept the at-least-25% FY27 growth guidance unchanged but said it expects to exceed it, with H1 revenue already up 45%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 order target of INR5,000 crores depends on water schemes tendering by March 2027 and on uneven water tendering and government fund-flow pressure, with JJM underspend of about INR20,000 crores.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is developing an OEM battery-pack business alongside EPC using a proprietary 104.4 kWh pack that has international certification, but no launch date or volume was given.

rows.label: BESS EPC conversion in FY27
rows.why: Management expects one more EPC conversion in FY27 (INR500-1,000 crores) from over INR8,000 crores of tenders bid, and the NTPC BESS order of INR1,128 crores is expected to deliver about INR300 crores of revenue in FY27.

rows.label: Large water schemes tendering by March 2027
rows.why: PKC link, Ken-Betwa, Wainganga-Nalganga and NVDA projects are expected to tender by March 2027, but management gave no firm dates and water is 65-70% of the order book.

rows.label: Arbitration award settlement
rows.why: About INR100 crores of awards across two matters are at a very advanced stage with settlement expected soon, which would reduce debt, but no fixed date was given against total claims of about INR3,827 crores.

tone.note: Management was confident on cash flow (H1 operating cash flow INR82.4 crores), margin protection and BESS demand, but cautious on order inflow timing and gave no firm dates for water tenders or arbitration settlement; analysts pressed on guidance revision and the sustainability of cash flow.
